cards.title: Schema discipline
items: tenant_id NOT NULL on every table, first column of every index and first term of every predicate, next to the standard columns id, created_at, updated_at, version, deleted_at
one schema per slice and no cross-slice foreign key or join — a cross-slice read goes through the other slice's contracts and a port
Flyway is the only schema authority and hbm2ddl.auto=validate in every deployed profile; migrations are a deploy step, never a startup task

cards.title: The write path
items: the domain row and the outbox row commit in one JTA transaction, so there is no window where the state changed and the event did not
the adapter sets app.tenant_id on the transaction before the first query and maps the entity to the domain at the repository boundary; no lazy proxy leaves the transaction
the JPA entity stays inside the adapter — the API receives a DTO record, and the use case sees a plain domain object

cards.title: Delivery and the second line
items: the worker claims the due rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, publishes and settles them; a failure backs off and ends in a dead-letter row an admin can see
the consumer deduplicates by the idempotency key because JMS delivers at-least-once; the key is UNIQUE in the schema, so a replay is a no-op
the RLS policy with a non-bypass application role filters again what the tenant predicate already selected — the database is the second line, never the first
